annotation.title_clean: Ethical Risks of Human–Robot Interaction in the Construction Industry: A Systematic Review
annotation.title_en: Ethical Risks of Human–Robot Interaction in the Construction Industry: A Systematic Review
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Wang, L.; Li, W.; Gu, B.; Li, N.; Fang, D.
annotation.venue: CIB Conferences (Proceedings of the 23rd CIB World Building Congress), Purdue e-Pubs
annotation.summary_en: PRISMA-based systematic review of ethical risks in human–robot interaction on construction sites, using an agent-relationship-scenario lens (managers, workers, robots; five interaction patterns). It identifies six risk dimensions and proposes ethical guidelines and normative recommendations to inform future administrative guidelines.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes an agent-relationship-scenario three-tier ethical lens for construction HRI
Identifies five HRI patterns: remote monitoring, proximity manipulation, non-collaborative coexistence, non-wearable and wearable collaboration
Finds six ethical risk dimensions: overtrust/distrust, human misconduct, robot misdesign, physical, psychological, regulation and accountability risks
Notes ethical research on construction HRI is scarce and too macro-level
Offers ethical guidelines and recommendations as a basis for administrative guidelines
